fix: ANSWER TO THE QUESTION ASKED -- the gate is NOT verdict-blocking, and my own prior recommendation for it is WRONG. I measured the fitted-span gate before recommending it again, and it must NOT be adopted. (1) WHY: the fitted span is not an independent quantity, it is ~ log10(C_hi/C_lo)/D2. Measured product fit_span_decades x D2 = 0.113-0.230 across FOURTEEN N=100 configurations spanning D2 from 2.0 to 149.9 -- uniform cubes d=2/3/5/8 give 0.176/0.176/0.154/0.151, iid Gaussians d=12/32/64/768 give 0.196/0.113/0.181/0.124, and the seven real models give 0.117-0.230 -- and 1.535-1.667 at N=2000. So a 0.05-decade FLOOR on the fitted window is algebraically a CEILING of D2 <~ 0.16/0.05 = 3.2 at N=100 (and <~32 at N=2000). That is the same class of gate as the Eckmann-Ruelle slope ceiling that was already deleted for censoring 14/14 real runs: it censors on the ANSWER, not on the data. (2) WHAT IT WOULD DO, measured: at N=100 it censors 40/40 uniform 8-cubes (median 6.3002 against a true 8) and 35/40 uniform 5-cubes (median 4.6570 against a true 5, only -6.9% off) while censoring 0/40 2-cubes -- it selects for LOW dimension, not for resolvability -- and it does not even separate real from pathological, since the 8-cube's fitted spans (0.0184-0.0373) overlap iid Gaussian d=12's (0.0138-0.0224). On the shipped configuration it is worse than I reported last round: with seven models the fitted spans are 0.0316/0.0241/0.0368/0.0328/0.0242/0.0550/0.0456, so it would censor FIVE of seven and pass pythia-410m and pythia-1b -- missing-not-at-random in a way correlated with the answer, which is more damaging than censoring all seven. So NO: censoring the shipped configuration on every model is NOT the right outcome. The shipped N=100 estimate IS underpowered (bootstrap sd 15-26%), but the fix for that is the point count, not a censoring rule that would equally discard an accurate 5-cube. (3) THE PAIR-COUNT FLOOR ALSO FAILS and I withdraw it too: pairs at the bottom of the fit are 171/99/46/105/189/75/54 for the seven models against 190/197/29-90 for iid Gaussian d=32/64/768, so a 100-pair floor would fail distilgpt2, opt-125m, pythia-410m and pythia-1b while PASSING iid Gaussian d=32 and d=64. The relative-standard-error form sqrt(2)/(sqrt(M_lo)*s_dec*ln10*D2) is D2-free for the same algebraic reason and reads 0.8% for every N=2000 cloud including iid Gaussian d=768 at 100.74, so it is blind to the pathology. (4) KEEP THE GATE ON THE FULL GRID. Of everything I measured, the full-grid span is the only quantity that is a property of the DATA rather than of the answer, and it is the only one that separates: 0.2149-0.4056 for the seven models and 0.2522-0.8474 for uniform cubes against 0.0157 for iid Gaussian d=768. It is loose at the margin (d=64 Gaussian passes at 0.0639 and returns 17.76) and that is worth tightening on measured separation, but the KEY is right. My prior finding survives only in weakened form -- as a DISCLOSURE defect, not a gating one: emit the fitted span alongside `_meta_correlation_dimension_min_decades` so the audit trail stops implying the floor bounds the fit. THEN, in severity order: (a) `_meta_`-prefix `hidden_state_correlation_dimension` and `correlation_dimension_scaling_region` (both are bit-identical aliases of `correlation_dimension`, and the uncensored twin already exists as `_meta_correlation_dimension_scaling_region_raw`) -- tests/tasks/test_comprehensive_parity.py:3194 and tests/tasks/test_geometry.py:720 read the alias and must be updated with it; (b) `_meta_`-prefix `fit_r_squared` (no other task emits that key) and keep the self-describing `correlation_dimension_scaling_r2` as the single R^2 feature; (c) call the plateau kernel BEFORE the percentile kernel's error returns, so a degenerate 5th percentile cannot suppress a headline the plateau can compute -- and either exclude zero distances from C(r)'s numerator or refuse when the coincident-pair fraction exceeds min_pairs_frac, since an atom in the cloud currently yields a confident near-zero slope at R^2 0.9959; (d) delete `_meta_correlation_dimension_eckmann_ruelle_slope_bound`, `n_points_est` and `d2_ceiling` -- an emitted threshold that nothing applies and that every reported value exceeds is worse than no threshold; (e) rewrite the module CALIBRATION CAVEAT and task_metadata.py:52, both of which still describe the demoted percentile kernel as the estimate; (f) plumb num_radii / min_window / min_pairs_frac / the 0.15 and 0.35 thresholds through the config and emit them, since none of the primary estimator's knobs is currently settable or recorded; (g) raise the default point count (pooling='all_tokens' or num_samples >= 2000): at N=100 the bootstrap sd is 15-26% of the value and every model roughly doubles at N=2000, which is the single change that would most improve this metric.
